_note: THE IMAGE MATRIX, AS DATA. Read by .github/workflows/build-ghcr.yml — both by the
input validator and by the plan job that builds the matrix for a dispatch.
★★ WHY IT LEFT THE YAML. The matrix used to live inline, and the validator read it back
out of the workflow file with sed. Two consequences, both observed:
1. A single-image dispatch still started EVERY leg. The per-leg skip was a step-level
`if:`, and GitHub downloads a job's actions during 'Set up job' — before any step
runs. So `-f image=interego-foxxi-bridge` spun up sixteen runners and pulled
docker/setup-buildx-action sixteen times, then skipped fifteen builds. Repeated
single-service deploys in one session earned 429 Too Many Requests from codeload and
failed five builds that had nothing wrong with them.
2. A job-level `if:` cannot fix it: the `matrix` context is not available there, and
trying it made the workflow unparseable (HTTP 422, caught on the next dispatch).
A matrix computed from THIS file by a plan job is the pattern that works: a dispatch for
one image expands to one leg, so no other runner starts and no other download happens.
★ AND ONE FILE RATHER THAN TWO COPIES. The validator's whole purpose is that a dispatch
which would build nothing must fail rather than go green; that only holds while it and the
matrix cannot disagree. Same file, same list, no sed parsing of YAML.
